claims.text: The hybrid CALPHAD–MLIP framework can accurately predict melting temperatures for refractory high-entropy alloys.
The hybrid framework can accurately predict entropy of fusion for refractory high-entropy alloys.
The hybrid framework can accurately predict heat capacity for refractory high-entropy alloys.
High-throughput CALPHAD can rapidly screen multicomponent composition spaces for phase stability.
Moment Tensor Potentials for Nb–Ta–Mo–W can be trained using DFT data spanning elemental, binary, ternary, and quaternary configurations.
Moment Tensor Potentials provide a favorable balance between DFT-level accuracy and computational cost.
MLIPs can capture complex SRO-dependent local-environment effects in refractory multicomponent alloys.
MLIPs capture SRO-induced variations in vibrational entropy and anharmonicity.
Standard empirical potentials such as EAM and MEAM fail to capture the multi-body interactions and SRO needed to predict melting properties.
Pure DFT is computationally prohibitive for screening vast RHEA composition spaces.
CALPHAD supplies a thermodynamically consistent phase-stability baseline for multicomponent alloys.
CALPHAD screening reduces the search space required for MLIP training and validation.
Chemical SRO and local lattice distortions modulate phonon spectra and anharmonic vibrational contributions to thermodynamic properties.
The proposed framework will predict RHEA melting temperatures within ±50 K.
The proposed framework will predict RHEA entropy of fusion within ±10%.
The proposed framework will predict RHEA heat capacity within ±5%.
The proposed framework will have computational cost orders of magnitude lower than pure DFT.
The methodology is valid only for single-phase BCC or FCC solid solutions in which SRO is the dominant microstructural feature.
An SRO parameter α greater than 0.5 is a valid quantitative boundary for applicability.
Systems with complex intermetallic precipitation or phase separation require explicit phase-field modeling and fall outside the method's validity.

contradictions.description: The initial-state field includes random solid solutions, whereas the boundary restricts validity to systems where SRO is dominant and α > 0.5; the hypothesis does not explain how a random state satisfies that boundary.

The claimed accuracies are substantially tighter than the falsification thresholds: ±50 K versus ±10% for melting temperature, ±10% versus ±15% for entropy of fusion, and ±5% versus ±10% for heat capacity. Results can therefore contradict the predicted outcome without falsifying the hypothesis under the stated test.
